name: SSC Subject Verb Agreement
description: Subject-verb agreement rules, traps, and examples for SSC English grammar.

cards.term: The list of items ___ on the table
cards.definition:
Correct answer: is

Rule: The subject is “list”, not “items”. A list is singular.

Example: The list of items is on the table like a tiny mountain of stationery.

cards.term: A bouquet of flowers ___ on the desk
cards.definition:
Correct answer: is

Rule: The subject is “bouquet”, not “flowers”. Bouquet is singular.

Example: A bouquet of flowers is on the desk, quietly making the office look less boring.

cards.term: A herd of cattle ___ moving slowly
cards.definition:
Correct answer: is

Rule: A collective noun is usually singular when treated as one unit.

Example: A herd of cattle is moving slowly across the dusty road.

cards.term: A number of students ___ absent today
cards.definition:
Correct answer: are

Rule: “A number of” means many, so it takes a plural verb.

Example: A number of students are absent today, which made the classroom suspiciously peaceful.

Correct answer: is

Rule: “The number of” refers to one figure, so it takes a singular verb.

Example: The number of students is increasing every year.

cards.term: Each of the boys ___ a notebook
cards.definition:
Correct answer: has

Rule: “Each” is singular.

Example: Each of the boys has a notebook, but only one has actually opened it.

cards.term: Every one of the answers ___ checked
cards.definition:
Correct answer: is

Rule: “Every one” is singular.

Example: Every one of the answers is checked before the final list is printed.

cards.term: Neither of the two plans ___ practical
cards.definition:
Correct answer: is

Rule: “Neither” is singular when referring to two options.

Example: Neither of the two plans is practical, which is impressive in a disappointing way.

cards.term: Either of the roads ___ safe at night
cards.definition:
Correct answer: is

Rule: “Either” is singular.

Example: Either of the roads is safe at night, but one has better street lights.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Indefinite pronoun “everyone” is singular.

Example: Everyone in the class is ready, except the student still looking for a pen.

Correct answer: is

Rule: “Everybody” is singular.

Example: Everybody is responsible for discipline, not just the monitor.

Correct answer: is

Rule: “Someone” is singular.

Example: Someone is knocking at the door with the confidence of a delivery agent.

Correct answer: has

Rule: “Somebody” is singular.

Example: Somebody has left a bag here, and now everyone suddenly looks innocent.

Correct answer: is

Rule: “Nobody” is singular.

Example: Nobody is above the law, not even the person who designed the form.

Correct answer: is

Rule: “No one” is singular.

Example: No one is allowed to enter without an admit card.

Correct answer: is

Rule: “Nothing” is singular.

Example: Nothing is impossible with practice, though grammar may pretend otherwise.

cards.term: Many a student ___ made this mistake
cards.definition:
Correct answer: has

Rule: “Many a” is followed by singular noun and singular verb.

Example: Many a student has made this mistake in error-spotting questions.

Correct answer: has

Rule: “More than one” usually takes a singular verb.

Example: More than one candidate has applied for the same post.

Correct answer: is

Rule: “One of” takes a singular verb because the subject is one.

Example: One of the players is injured, and the coach is already calculating excuses.

cards.term: The quality of these mangoes ___ excellent
cards.definition:
Correct answer: is

Rule: The subject is “quality”, singular.

Example: The quality of these mangoes is excellent, according to the uncle who tasted five.

Correct answer: are

Rule: The subject “prices” is plural.

Example: The prices of petrol are rising faster than morning motivation.

Correct answer: is

Rule: “News” is singular despite ending in s.

Example: The news is shocking, and the WhatsApp version is probably worse.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Names of subjects ending in s are usually singular.

Example: Mathematics is my favourite subject when the answer comes out clean.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Academic subjects are singular.

Example: Physics is difficult until the diagram finally starts making sense.

Correct answer: is

Rule: When politics means a field of study or activity, it is singular.

Example: Politics is often complicated because everyone thinks they are the expert.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Academic subjects take singular verbs.

Example: Economics is useful when people stop treating money like magic.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Names of diseases ending in s are usually singular.

Example: Measles is a contagious disease, not a plural group of diseases.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Disease names ending in s are singular.

Example: Mumps is common among children.

Correct answer: are

Rule: Tools with two parts often take plural verbs.

Example: The scissors are sharp enough to scare the wrapping paper.

Correct answer: are

Rule: Clothing items with two parts take plural verbs.

Example: The trousers are too loose after his diet actually worked.

Correct answer: are

Rule: Spectacles are treated as plural.

Example: My spectacles are broken, so the blackboard has become abstract art.

Correct answer: is

Rule: “A pair of” is singular.

Example: A pair of scissors is missing, probably hiding under the craft paper.

cards.term: A pair of shoes ___ near the door
cards.definition:
Correct answer: is

Rule: “A pair” is singular.

Example: A pair of shoes is near the door, announcing that someone has arrived.

Correct answer: are

Rule: “Police” is treated as plural.

Example: The police are investigating the case with unusual patience.

cards.term: The cattle ___ grazing in the field
cards.definition:
Correct answer: are

Rule: “Cattle” is plural.

Example: The cattle are grazing in the field as if exams do not exist.

Correct answer: are

Rule: “People” is plural.

Example: The people are angry because the queue moved backwards.

cards.term: The public ___ divided on the issue
cards.definition:
Correct answer: is

Rule: “Public” as a collective body is usually singular.

Example: The public is divided on the issue, as usual.

Correct answer: has

Rule: A committee acting as one unit takes a singular verb.

Example: The committee has reached a decision after only three cups of tea.

Correct answer: are

Rule: A collective noun takes plural verb when members act separately.

Example: The committee are arguing among themselves, which explains the delay.

Correct answer: is

Rule: A team as one unit takes singular verb.

Example: The team is playing well today.

cards.term: The team ___ wearing different practice kits
cards.definition:
Correct answer: are

Rule: When individual members are emphasized, plural verb may be used.

Example: The team are wearing different practice kits because nobody read the message.

cards.term: Bread and butter ___ his favourite breakfast
cards.definition:
Correct answer: is

Rule: When two nouns form one idea or dish, use singular verb.

Example: Bread and butter is his favourite breakfast.

Correct answer: is

Rule: One combined dish or idea takes singular verb.

Example: Rice and curry is served here every afternoon.

Correct answer: is

Rule: If one person holds both roles, singular verb is used.

Example: The principal and secretary is present because both titles belong to one person.

cards.term: The principal and the secretary ___ present
cards.definition:
Correct answer: are

Rule: Two different people take plural verb.

Example: The principal and the secretary are present in the meeting.

cards.term: A black and white cow ___ grazing
cards.definition:
Correct answer: is

Rule: One cow with two colours takes singular verb.

Example: A black and white cow is grazing near the pond.

cards.term: A black and a white cow ___ grazing
cards.definition:
Correct answer: are

Rule: Two cows take plural verb.

Example: A black and a white cow are grazing near the pond.

Correct answer: wins

Rule: A phrase treated as one idea takes singular verb.

Example: Slow and steady wins the race, though fast and panicked tries hard.

cards.term: Early to bed and early to rise ___ a healthy habit
cards.definition:
Correct answer: is

Rule: The whole proverb-like idea is singular.

Example: Early to bed and early to rise is a healthy habit.

Correct answer: is

Rule: One person described by two titles takes singular verb.

Example: The poet and philosopher is dead if both titles refer to the same person.

cards.term: The poet and the philosopher ___ dead
cards.definition:
Correct answer: are

Rule: Two different people take plural verb.

Example: The poet and the philosopher are dead if the titles refer to two persons.

Correct answer: is

Rule: With “neither...nor”, verb agrees with the nearer subject. Here “Shyam” is singular.

Example: Neither Ram nor Shyam is present, so the excuse factory is closed.

cards.term: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ ready
cards.definition:
Correct answer: are

Rule: Verb agrees with nearer subject “students”.

Example: Neither the teacher nor the students are ready for the surprise test.

cards.term: Neither the students nor the teacher ___ ready
cards.definition:
Correct answer: is

Rule: Verb agrees with nearer subject “teacher”.

Example: Neither the students nor the teacher is ready for the surprise inspection.

cards.term: Either my friends or my brother ___ coming
cards.definition:
Correct answer: is

Rule: Verb agrees with nearer subject “brother”.

Example: Either my friends or my brother is coming to help.

cards.term: Either my brother or my friends ___ coming
cards.definition:
Correct answer: are

Rule: Verb agrees with nearer subject “friends”.

Example: Either my brother or my friends are coming to help.

cards.term: Not only the manager but also the clerks ___ responsible
cards.definition:
Correct answer: are

Rule: With paired conjunctions, verb agrees with nearer subject.

Example: Not only the manager but also the clerks are responsible.

cards.term: Not only the clerks but also the manager ___ responsible
cards.definition:
Correct answer: is

Rule: Verb agrees with nearer subject “manager”.

Example: Not only the clerks but also the manager is responsible.

cards.term: The captain, along with his players, ___ ready
cards.definition:
Correct answer: is

Rule: Words like “along with” do not change the subject.

Example: The captain, along with his players, is ready for the final.

cards.term: The teacher, as well as the students, ___ excited
cards.definition:
Correct answer: is

Rule: “As well as” does not make the subject plural.

Example: The teacher, as well as the students, is excited about the trip.

cards.term: The minister, together with his officers, ___ arriving
cards.definition:
Correct answer: is

Rule: “Together with” does not affect the main subject.

Example: The minister, together with his officers, is arriving soon.

cards.term: The boy, besides his friends, ___ guilty
cards.definition:
Correct answer: is

Rule: “Besides” phrase does not change the singular subject.

Example: The boy, besides his friends, is guilty of breaking the window.

Correct answer: am

Rule: Verb agrees with the real subject “I”.

Example: I, not my brother, am responsible for the missing charger.

Correct answer: are

Rule: Verb agrees with “you”.

Example: You, not he, are to blame for the delay.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Verb agrees with “he”.

Example: He, not they, is chosen for the role.

cards.term: There ___ a book on the table
cards.definition:
Correct answer: is

Rule: In “there” sentences, verb agrees with the real subject after it.

Example: There is a book on the table, exactly where nobody looked.

cards.term: There ___ many books on the table
cards.definition:
Correct answer: are

Rule: Verb agrees with plural subject “books”.

Example: There are many books on the table.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Verb agrees with singular subject “answer”.

Example: Here is the answer you were searching for.

Correct answer: are

Rule: Verb agrees with plural subject “documents”.

Example: Here are the documents for verification.

cards.term: The cost of these items ___ high
cards.definition:
Correct answer: is

Rule: Subject is “cost”, singular.

Example: The cost of these items is high enough to make the wallet nervous.

cards.term: The results of the test ___ declared
cards.definition:
Correct answer: are

Rule: Subject is “results”, plural.

Example: The results of the test are declared online.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Fraction of uncountable singular noun takes singular verb.

Example: One-third of the work is complete.

Correct answer: are

Rule: Fraction of plural noun takes plural verb.

Example: One-third of the students are absent.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Fraction of singular uncountable/whole noun takes singular verb.

Example: Half of the cake is gone, and the birthday boy looks suspicious.

Correct answer: are

Rule: Fraction of plural noun takes plural verb.

Example: Half of the apples are rotten.

Correct answer: is

Rule: “Water” is uncountable, so singular verb.

Example: Some of the water is dirty.

Correct answer: are

Rule: “Books” is plural, so plural verb.

Example: Some of the books are missing.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Money as an amount is singular.

Example: All of the money is spent, and the month is still young.

Correct answer: are

Rule: Coins are countable plural.

Example: All of the coins are lost under the sofa.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Information is uncountable, so singular.

Example: Most of the information is useful.

Correct answer: are

Rule: Questions are plural.

Example: Most of the questions are easy.

Correct answer: is

Rule: With uncountable noun, “none” takes singular verb.

Example: None of the milk is left.

Correct answer: are

Rule: With plural noun, “none” often takes plural verb in modern usage.

Example: None of the boys are ready for the race.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Distance as a single amount takes singular verb.

Example: Five kilometres is a long distance on a hot afternoon.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Money amount as a unit takes singular verb.

Example: Ten rupees is not enough for lunch anymore.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Time period as a single amount takes singular verb.

Example: Two hours is enough for revision if the phone stays away.

cards.term: Fifty percent of the work ___ done
cards.definition:
Correct answer: is

Rule: Percent of singular/uncountable noun takes singular verb.

Example: Fifty percent of the work is done.

cards.term: Fifty percent of the students ___ present
cards.definition:
Correct answer: are

Rule: Percent of plural noun takes plural verb.

Example: Fifty percent of the students are present.

cards.term: The United States ___ a large country
cards.definition:
Correct answer: is

Rule: Country names that look plural take singular verb.

Example: The United States is a large country.

cards.term: The Arabian Nights ___ a famous book
cards.definition:
Correct answer: is

Rule: Titles of books take singular verb.

Example: The Arabian Nights is a famous book.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Book title takes singular verb.

Example: Gulliver's Travels is interesting.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Some fixed expressions take singular verb by sense.

Example: The wages of sin is death is a traditional expression.

Correct answer: are

Rule: “Means” can be plural when referring to resources.

Example: His means are limited.

Correct answer: is

Rule: “Means” as method can be singular.

Example: This means is useful in solving the problem.

Correct answer: is

Rule: “Headquarters” may be singular when referring to one office.

Example: The headquarters is in Delhi.

Correct answer: are

Rule: “Premises” meaning building/land is plural.

Example: The premises are guarded at night.

Correct answer: are

Rule: “Data” is traditionally plural, though singular use is common. SSC often expects plural.

Example: The data are reliable in formal grammar.

Correct answer: is

Rule: “Datum” is singular of data.

Example: The datum is reliable.

Correct answer: are

Rule: “Media” is traditionally plural of medium.

Example: Media are powerful today in formal grammar.

Correct answer: is

Rule: “Medium” is singular.

Example: The medium is effective for communication.

Correct answer: are

Rule: “Criteria” is plural.

Example: Criteria are important in selection.

Correct answer: is

Rule: “Criterion” is singular.

Example: One criterion is important in this test.

Correct answer: are

Rule: “Phenomena” is plural.

Example: These phenomena are difficult to explain.

Correct answer: is

Rule: “Phenomenon” is singular.

Example: This phenomenon is rare.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Audience as one group takes singular verb.

Example: The audience is silent before the final scene.

Correct answer: are

Rule: When individual members are emphasized, plural verb may be used.

Example: The audience are leaving their seats one by one.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Jury acting as one body takes singular verb.

Example: The jury is unanimous.

cards.term: The jury ___ divided in their opinions
cards.definition:
Correct answer: are

Rule: Jury members acting separately take plural verb.

Example: The jury are divided in their opinions.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Staff as one unit can be singular.

Example: The staff is efficient.

Correct answer: are

Rule: Members acting individually take plural verb.

Example: The staff are arguing among themselves.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Furniture is uncountable, so singular verb.

Example: The furniture is old but still strong.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Luggage is uncountable, so singular verb.

Example: The luggage is heavy enough to count as gym training.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Information is uncountable.

Example: The information is correct.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Advice is uncountable.

Example: The advice is useful.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Machinery is uncountable.

Example: The machinery is expensive.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Equipment is uncountable.

Example: The equipment is new.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Scenery is uncountable.

Example: The scenery is beautiful.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Poetry as a subject/collection is singular.

Example: The poetry of Kabir is inspiring.

Correct answer: are

Rule: Poems are plural.

Example: The poems of Kabir are inspiring.

Correct answer: is

Rule: A noun clause as subject takes singular verb.

Example: What he said is true.

Correct answer: is

Rule: The clause “what they need” is singular in sense.

Example: What they need is books, not another lecture.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Infinitive phrase as subject is singular.

Example: To err is human.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Gerund as subject takes singular verb.

Example: Swimming is good exercise.

Correct answer: improves

Rule: Gerund phrase as subject is singular.

Example: Reading books improves vocabulary.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Gerund phrase is singular.

Example: Collecting stamps is his hobby.

Correct answer: are

Rule: Adjective used as class takes plural verb.

Example: The rich are not always happy.

cards.term: The poor ___ helped by the scheme
cards.definition:
Correct answer: are

Rule: Adjective used as class takes plural verb.

Example: The poor are helped by the scheme.

Correct answer: are

Rule: Adjective used as a class takes plural verb.

Example: The honest are respected in every age.

Correct answer: is

Rule: If one accused person is meant, singular verb is used.

Example: The accused is present in court.

Correct answer: am

Rule: With “I”, use “am” in present continuous.

Example: I am going to the market.

Correct answer: has

Rule: With singular third person, use “has”.

Example: He has completed the task before the deadline.

Correct answer: have

Rule: With plural subject, use “have”.

Example: They have completed the task.

Correct answer: does

Rule: Use “does” with singular third person.

Example: She does not like spicy food.

Correct answer: do

Rule: Use “do” with plural subject.

Example: They do not like spicy food.

Correct answer: is

Rule: Singular subject takes singular helping verb.

Example: The boy is playing outside.

Correct answer: are

Rule: Plural subject takes plural helping verb.

Example: The boys are playing outside.

Correct answer: has

Rule: If one person is both friend and guide, singular verb.

Example: My friend and guide has arrived.

cards.term: My friend and my guide ___ arrived
cards.definition:
Correct answer: have

Rule: If two people are meant, plural verb.

Example: My friend and my guide have arrived.

cards.term: Each boy and each girl ___ given a prize
cards.definition:
Correct answer: was

Rule: “Each...and each” takes singular verb.

Example: Each boy and each girl was given a prize.

cards.term: Every teacher and every student ___ invited
cards.definition:
Correct answer: is

Rule: “Every...and every” takes singular verb.

Example: Every teacher and every student is invited.

cards.term: No teacher and no student ___ allowed inside
cards.definition:
Correct answer: is

Rule: “No...and no” with singular nouns takes singular verb.

Example: No teacher and no student is allowed inside without permission.

Correct answer: have

Rule: Plural subject takes plural verb.

Example: Many students have applied for the scholarship.

cards.term: Many a flower ___ born to blush unseen
cards.definition:
Correct answer: is

Rule: “Many a” takes singular verb.

Example: Many a flower is born to blush unseen.
